subject.title: [Bug P2] scheduleReconnect() has no max retry limit — infinite reconnect loop

question: Should GatewayClient keep unlimited reconnects by default with an opt-in cap for short-lived callers, or should OpenClaw change the default reconnect policy globally?
rationale: The unbounded scheduler is source-reproducible, but node-host recovery intentionally benefits from indefinite reconnects, so the retry contract is a compatibility and product decision.

options.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
options.body: Keep existing long-lived clients unlimited by default, add the cap in the package client, and wire it only into caller paths maintainers approve as short-lived.

options.title: Global retry cap
options.body: Stop every GatewayClient after a fixed number of attempts, accepting that node hosts may not recover automatically after extended gateway outages.

options.title: Document unlimited retry as intended
options.body: Keep the current retry model and close the report only if maintainers explicitly accept the resource-risk tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Opt-in bounded reconnect
recommendation.body: Keep existing long-lived clients unlimited by default, add the cap in the package client, and wire it only into caller paths maintainers approve as short-lived.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is tied to the original Gateway WebSocket client behavior and is the best available owner for the reconnect contract decision.
